articles.title: Americast - Has Pete Hegseth lost control of the Pentagon? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: The US military is losing its senior leaders.
articles.body: Why is the US military losing its senior leaders? In the latest in a series of high-profile departures inside the Pentagon, America’s top civilian official Dan Driscoll has resigned as Army Secretary having been appointed 18 months ago by Donald Trump to help end the Ukraine war and modernise US forces. In this episode, Anthony and Sumi discuss the significance of the resignation and the real reasons behind it. Driscoll’s departure comes after Pete Hegseth has fired or forced out senior officers across nearly every service, including the chairman of the Joint Chiefs, the Navy’s top admiral and the Army chief of staff. But six months into the Iran war, the Pentagon is dealing with fewer senior leaders, few munitions and further questions about the way in which Hegseth is running operations. Meanwhile, there are also concerns about morale. USS Abraham Lincoln, an aircraft carrier with nearly 5,000 personnel aboard, is finally due to dock in Pattaya, Thailand, after a record 250 days at sea without a port stop. There’s been scrutiny of conditions on the carrier after members of Congress raised concerns about conditions on the ship and mental stress among the crew. It’s the largest number of US personnel to visit Pattaya since the fall of Saigon in 1975 at the end of the Vietnam War. articles.title: How will El Niño affect the weather in the UK?
articles.summary: This year's El Niño is expected to be the strongest in living memory and could lead to a range of impacts of the UK - including a stormy autumn.
articles.body:
El Niño is developing right now across the Pacific Ocean - thousands of miles away from the UK.

Its most profound impacts may well be centred around this area, with the increased risk of flooding and landslides in Peru and Ecuador and the threat of droughts and wildfires in Australia.

However the disruption caused to global wind patterns means the impacts will ripple right across the globe.

And the Met Office says the UK weather is likely to be affected, with the growing chance that autumn and early winter will be wet and stormy.

No two El Niños are the same - so, while it may increase the chance of certain types of weather occurring, this is not guaranteed.

El Niño set to be 'strongest in living memory', says Met Office

"I have not seen an event like this developing in our forecasts before", said Professor Adam Scaife, head of long-range forecasts at the Met Office.

He says the scale of the growing El Niño is unprecedented in modern climate records.

As it approaches its peak by the end of 2026, its influence around the world will grow with effects spreading across the globe.

Professor Scaife says forecasters "already see signals for increased rainfall and storminess in autumn here in the UK", especially into November and December.

After a summer that looks set to be the UK's hottest on record and with the drought conditions that continue to grip large swathes of the country, a wet autumn sounds like good news.

However, we know that climate change is making increasingly intense rainfall more likely, and so these storms and downpours will also bring the threat of flooding.

Strong winds could also cause damage, transport disruption and power cuts.

The winter of 2015 and 2016, which coincided with a very strong El Niño, brought a succession of major storms delivering what experts at the time described as the most extreme flooding on record .

El Niño can be associated with cold spells in the late winter - but the link is not a strong one and the past evidence is mixed.

The so-called Big Freeze of winter 2009/2010 was, at the time, the coldest in three decades - and this coincided with an El Niño.

However, 2006/2007 was also an El Niño winter and that was unseasonably warm.

The further forecasters look into the future the more uncertain the prospects become.

So while El Niño may increase the chance of cold weather early in 2027, this is not guaranteed.

Globally, a very strong El Niño typically lifts average temperatures by 0.2C.

This may not sound like much, but on top of the heating effect of human-induced climate change it will increase the risks of heatwaves around the world.

However, El Niño's effects are not the same in each individual place, and the links to hot weather in the UK are not clear.

"Long-term global warming remains the more significant driver of the UK's rising temperatures and increasing risk of extreme heat" said Dr Akshay Deoras, a climate scientist at the University of Reading.

"It is still too early to say what next summer will bring for the UK", added Dr Deoras, "however El Niño's additional warming, coupled with the UK's already warmer climate, could provide the conditions for a hot summer."

articles.title: Low-effort relationships: We are simply too exhausted to love
articles.summary: Amit Mehra, a software engineer based out of Gurugram, has been trying to zero in on a day to have a quiet evening with his wife for the past five mon.
articles.body: Amit Mehra, a software engineer based out of Gurugram, has been trying to zero in on a day to have a quiet evening with his wife for the past five months. Nothing urgent. There's no thundering crisis. It's just that in the daily grind, he and his wife of 14 years, Sonali, have been feeling the distance for a while now. "I can feel it, and so can Sonali," says Amit. But he's exhausted. So they both have gotten used to just doing the bare minimum needed to keep their relationship alive — maybe a dinner here, a movie there — but the distance doesn't seem to close. Experts are calling this a "low-effort relationship".Not falling out of love, running out of energyYes, it sounds demeaning. It sounds insulting. It also sounds as if couples these days are not willing to put in the work that's needed to keep love and relationships alive. But thinking that wouldn't just be judgmental, it would be wrong. Low-effort relationships aren't the result of couples falling out of love. Increasingly, experts say, it's because they have run out of energy.Burnout has long been discussed in the context of work. We know it affects productivity, mental health and physical well-being. But we hardly talk about how it's affecting our personal lives. Relationships these days aren't ending with slammed doors, dramatic fights or heartbreaking betrayals. They are simply fading.One forgotten anniversary becomes two. Date nights are replaced by "maybe, next weekend." Conversations shrink into logistical updates about groceries, bills and school pickups. At bedtime, two people lie inches apart, each illuminated by the blue glow of their own phone, scrolling through different worlds.Like Mehra, Ankita Sharma, a brand collaborator with a media house, has seen her relationship with her husband Sumit just decline for "no apparent reason". "Whenever I feel like bringing up the subject, I choke up. I feel like instead of addressing it like a mature adult, I'll just start to scream and cry."The butterfly and the reelClinical nutritionist and wellness consultant Dr Ananya Bhowmik has seen this all too often in the past few years. "It's not just relationships. This extreme exhaustion leading to minimal effort among couples in a relationship is hurting them physically too." Some stop eating, some binge eat for emotional comfort. "At times, even after losing considerable weight, a patient would not look happy at all. That spark of life that kept people happy seems to be gone these days," she says.Dr Bhowmik explains in very simple terms what she thinks is happening to us personally due to burnout. Says she, "Let's say, you see a yellow butterfly sitting on an orange flower. It immediately lifts your mood because you are seeing this nature's wonder with your own eyes. That gives a certain amount of stimulus to your nervous system."But when you see that same thing on a reel, it will not stimulate you similarly. The most tricky and dangerous part here is though you won't feel the stimulus like you did in natural surroundings, your mind will perceive the reel or slow-motion video of the same butterfly on the same flower as a 'happy moment'."That's what is happening with low-effort relationships too. The effort is there, but also not there. And eventually, it seems fake. Because it's not giving us the simple happiness of being together, like we've seen our parents enjoy.Adds Dr Bhowmik, "Millennials, and to some extent even Gen Z, have seen real relationships and happy times when it came to their parents. They are expecting to feel the same authenticity but the pressures of modern life is such a huge wall between couples that it is becoming an insurmountable problem. It's only the last 15 years or so that smart gadgets have completely taken over our lives. The thing is we haven't forgotten what authenticity feels like, and we are trying to recreate it with whatever minimum energy modern life allows us for relationships. But it's not enough to feel the love."The 'low' in low-effort relationships is not by choice; it's just the reality of a 24x7 connected life we have today. When you are sitting and talking to each other, looking at each other's eyes, and you can chat for hours without realising that it's been one hour, that is what this generation is missing.Bhowmik adds, "The tragic part is we all had the taste of it before. We probably did not know how much it helped us bond, but our senses were wired like that. We were, in general, happy people because we had human touch and human connection. Texts, smileys, and heart emojis, at the end of the day, are poor substitutes for an hour of just really looking into each other's eyes, listening to one another and laughing at old jokes."When burnout follows you homeBelgian psychotherapist and author Esther Perel has long argued that routine, domestic responsibilities and ongoing stress dampen desire, and that when emotional energy is drained by work and household demands, partners tend to prioritise safety and quiet routines over romance.Today, burnout doesn't stop at the office door. It follows us home, settling quietly into our closest relationships. After a day of endless notifications, packed schedules, financial worries and emotional overload, many couples simply don't have the bandwidth for the kind of attention love quietly demands.Love, after all, isn't sustained by grand declarations. It survives on small everyday acts or regular catch-up moments between couples, even if it's for 20 minutes. Remembering how your partner takes their coffee, asking how the meeting went and actually listening to the answer, looking up from your phone when they're telling you about their day. These moments appear insignificant, but relationship researchers have long argued that they form the invisible architecture of intimacy.When they disappear, relationships don't just collapse overnight. They slowly become functional rather than fulfilling. Says Dr Santosh Bangar, senior consultant psychiatrist, Gleneagles Hospital, Mumbai, "Burnout may not have a direct impact on the relationship, but may slowly weaken the emotional connection between partners due to the failure to address the situation." Possibly, even the failure to recognise it.Our 'parallel scrolling' livesThe most visible version of this shift is what therapists call parallel scrolling. Couples settle into bed after work, not to reconnect, but to disconnect together. One watches short videos, the other checks emails or social media. Hours pass in silence. They are physically together, emotionally elsewhere.Technology often gets the blame, but the phone is more symptom than cause. Scrolling has become the easiest form of recovery after mentally exhausting days. Unfortunately, it also becomes the easiest way to avoid conversation, vulnerability and emotional presence.Too many roles, too little left overModern relationships are also carrying a heavier emotional load than ever before. Today's couples aren't just partners. They are expected to be best friends, co-parents, financial planners, therapists and career supporters all at once.At the same time, many are navigating economic uncertainty, rising living costs, demanding jobs and shrinking support systems. The expectations have expanded, but the emotional resources haven't. So we may genuinely love our partners and still consistently fail to make them feel loved.It usually shows up first in the texting, where messages turn transactional:Did you pay the electricity bill?Can you pick up milk?Who's collecting the kids?Even couples without children notice conversations revolving around logistics rather than curiosity. Weeks pass without asking questions like: What's been on your mind lately? What are you excited about these days?Emotional neglect doesn't always look like indifference. Often, it's just exhaustion. This helps explain why many people describe feeling lonely inside otherwise stable relationships. They are simply living with partners who are emotionally depleted. As are they. The affection is still there, buried beneath deadlines, sleep deprivation and an endless list of responsibilities.Intimacy stubbornly refuses to be efficientWe live in an era obsessed with efficiency. We optimise our workdays, automate our homes and outsource countless daily tasks. Yet intimacy stubbornly refuses to become efficient. Relationships cannot be sustained through shortcuts or multitasking, and presence cannot be automated.Psychologists often distinguish between time spent together and quality attention. Couples may technically spend hours in the same room, yet never truly connect. Simply occupying the same physical space doesn't nourish emotional intimacy. Eye contact, active listening, shared laughter and uninterrupted conversation do.No alarm bells announcing a breakdownThe danger of low-effort relationships is that they rarely trigger alarm bells. There is no obvious crisis demanding attention. Instead, partners slowly adapt to emotional distance until it becomes normal. They stop expecting affection because disappointment feels more exhausting than acceptance. One day, someone says, "I don't know when we stopped being us."Adds Dr Bangar, "If someone is constantly stressed or exhausted, he/she will be irritated, fatigued, have less patience, feel frustrated, avoid meaningful conversations, forget important moments, or spend more time on their own rather than with each other. This leads to issues like loneliness, misunderstandings, and emotional distance from the partner which is concerning. Hence, it is imperative for couples to get regular breaks, strike a work-life balance, spend quality time with each other, appreciate each other's company to rekindle the relationship and re-discover lost emotional connection."What actually helpsThe encouraging news is that relationships usually don't require extraordinary gestures to recover. In fact, the opposite may be true. Research consistently suggests that consistent, everyday moments of connection matter more than expensive holidays or elaborate surprises.A ten-minute walk after dinner without phones. Morning tea together before the day begins, a few extra seconds in a hug, one meaningful question before bed, looking at each other instead of at another screen. None of this is revolutionary. It is just attention.Perhaps that's what makes the low-effort relationship such an important cultural conversation. It challenges the comforting belief that love naturally sustains itself once commitment is established. Burnout may be unavoidable in a life like this one, but what it does to a relationship is not.Dr Bhowmik says another significant factor behind low-effort relationships is that there is no work-life balance among couples today. "That demarcation has to be brought back as an emergency. Not just for couples to survive a relationship. But to find ourselves, our own souls. It is not a cliche when people say 'take care of yourself, so that you can take care of another'."So the real question is whether low-effort relationships are on the rise because we have also developed a low-effort relationship with ourselves. After all, it is difficult to bring presence, intimacy and tenderness to another person when we have so little left for ourselves. That is a story for another day though.Looking for trusted parenting advice? Follow TOI Parenting Circle on Instagram for expert guidance, relatable stories, and practical tips delivered every day.

articles.title: A 'cidade do pecado' onde militares dos EUA atracaram  | G1
articles.standfirst: Após 250 dias no mar, o USS Abraham Lincoln atracou perto de Pattaya, cidade conhecida por sua agitada vida noturna e turismo sexual.
articles.summary: Após 250 dias no mar, o USS Abraham Lincoln atracou perto de Pattaya, cidade conhecida por sua agitada vida noturna e turismo sexual.
articles.body:
Pattaya, Tailândia — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

Após um período recorde de 250 dias no mar sem parada em um porto, o porta-aviões nuclear americano USS Abraham Lincoln atracou na Tailândia nesta quarta-feira (2).

A parada perto da cidade tailandesa de Pattaya proporciona aos quase 5 mil fuzileiros navais dos EUA um descanso muito esperado.

Pattaya é famosa por sua vibrante vida noturna e pelo turismo sexual, o que lhe rendeu o apelido de "Cidade do Pecado".

Esse rótulo, frequentemente usado pela mídia, é rejeitado pelas autoridades tailandesas.

Para os militares dos EUA, Pattaya evoca fortes memórias históricas.

Quando os marinheiros cansados ​​entrarem nos bares e restaurantes da cidade, estarão seguindo os passos das centenas de milhares de soldados americanos que foram para lá em busca de descanso e lazer durante a Guerra do Vietnã.

Sua presença transformou o local, que passou de uma tranquila vila de pescadores a uma das cidades mais famosas e frenéticas do mundo para festas.

Hoje, os becos iluminados com néon que levam à praia estão muito mais tranquilos do que o normal.

Os bares da famosa rua de pedestres da cidade — a Walking Street — ainda projetam vídeos de mulheres dançando, numa tentativa de atrair visitantes.

No entanto, não há muitos clientes. Os visitantes parecem ser na maioria famílias do Oriente Médio, mais interessadas no vendedor de sorvete turco do que nas casas noturnas.

A guerra dos EUA com o Irã afetou o turismo e o consumo, prejudicando duramente os negócios locais.

Fuzileiros navais americanos chegando ao Hard Rock Hotel em Pattaya — Foto: Reuters via BBC

Agora, a perspectiva de receber milhares de fuzileiros navais americanos, que economizaram seus salários no mar durante quase nove meses, é uma oportunidade excepcional para os negócios da região.

O porta-aviões americano partiu de San Diego em novembro passado para uma missão que inicialmente estava planejada para durar seis meses no Pacífico e no Mar da China Meridional.

No entanto, o navio foi desviado para o Golfo Pérsico depois que os Estados Unidos e Israel iniciaram operações militares contra o Irã no final de fevereiro.

Recentemente, membros do Congresso dos EUA expressaram preocupação com relatos de escassez de alimentos a bordo do navio, banheiros com defeito e estresse psicológico entre a tripulação.

A Marinha dos EUA reconheceu que as condições de trabalho têm sido difíceis , mas garantiu que a tripulação recebe apoio adequado.

No entanto, recusou-se a comentar à BBC sobre a parada do porta-aviões em Pattaya, alegando razões de segurança operacional.

O porta-aviões USS Abraham Lincoln atracou em Pattaya após 250 dias no mar — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

Apesar de sua estreita relação com a China, a Tailândia é aliada dos EUA por meio de tratados bilaterais. Visitas de navios da Marinha americana aos seus portos são comuns.

No entanto, este é provavelmente o maior contingente militar americano a chegar diretamente de uma zona de guerra a Pattaya desde a queda de Saigon em 1975.

A guerra no Irã está afetando os negócios locais em Pattaya — Foto: Lulu Luo/BBC

"Esta visita pode ser nossa maior esperança", comemora Anon Saiteer, um vendedor de joias em uma loja perto da Walking Street.

O estabelecimento colocou uma grande placa dando as boas-vindas aos fuzileiros navais americanos e oferecendo-lhes um desconto especial.

"Não temos nada a perder; só esperamos que eles gastem algum dinheiro aqui", diz o vendedor.

No entanto, as autoridades americanas e tailandesas estão tentando garantir que isso aconteça sem gerar as manchetes sensacionalistas pelas quais Pattaya ficou conhecida.

As autoridades tailandesas determinaram que a presença de militares americanos é proibida em alguns lugares.

Uma delas é a Soi 6, uma rua que leva à praia principal e é conhecida pela concentração de bares de strip-tease .

Embora a polícia tailandesa tenha lembrado aos visitantes americanos que a prostituição é tecnicamente ilegal na Tailândia , estima-se que existam entre 25 mil e 50 mil profissionais do sexo na cidade.

Muitas delas trabalham na Soi 6, onde se exibem em frente aos bares, convidando homens a entrar.

As numerosas lojas de cannabis de Pattaya também são proibidas para os militares americanos, assim como alguns esportes aquáticos, como parasailing e jet ski .

Embora a prostituição seja ilegal na Tailândia, locais turísticos e badalados como a Walking Street estão repletos de profissionais do sexo — Foto: Reuters via BBC

"É uma decisão deles", declarou o prefeito Poramase Ngampiches à BBC.

"Os militares americanos fizeram a sua lição de casa", acrescentou, ironicamente.

O adido naval americano Kristopher Robinson esquivou-se das perguntas da BBC sobre as atividades proibidas para os militares.

Em vez disso, afirmou que as tropas americanas "se comportarão de acordo com a lei americana, os regulamentos da Marinha dos EUA e a lei tailandesa".

"Tentamos proporcionar aos marinheiros o máximo de oportunidades de descanso possível", disse Robinson.

A Marinha dos EUA organizou um serviço de ônibus entre o porto e Pattaya das 5h às 2h da manhã, durante toda a estadia do porta-aviões na Tailândia . Dois hotéis também foram disponibilizados para os tripulantes americanos que desejarem pernoitar em terra.

As autoridades tailandesas mobilizaram centenas de policiais para monitorar as áreas de entretenimento da cidade e alertaram os comerciantes locais para que não cobrem preços abusivos dos turistas americanos.

"As visitas de militares americanos há 50 ou 60 anos colocaram Pattaya no mapa mundial e a transformaram em uma atração turística", diz o prefeito Poramase.

"Sejamos honestos: a cidade é conhecida pelas garotas de programa. Entendemos os estigmas. Não podemos evitá-los", reconhece.

"O que podemos fazer é mostrar que Pattaya mudou e que agora oferece outras opções, como esportes, seminários, programas de bem-estar e atividades para toda a família. É uma mistura de tudo."

Ambos os países esperam que, quando o USS Abraham Lincoln iniciar sua longa viagem de volta para casa pelo Pacífico em 6 de setembro, sua tripulação esteja revigorada e descansada.

Localizada a cerca de 100 quilômetros de Bangkok, Pattaya era uma pequena vila de pescadores em meados do século 20.

Os primeiros militares americanos chegaram em 1959, quando fuzileiros navais estacionados nas proximidades começaram a usar suas praias para descanso, de acordo com registros municipais citados em um estudo de 2024 das Universidades de Thammasat e Chulalongkorn.

No entanto, foi durante a Guerra do Vietnã que a transformação radical de Pattaya começou.

A cidade se tornou um ponto parada para os militares enviados para o Vietnã, relativamente próximo à Tailândia , embora os países não compartilhem uma fronteira terrestre.

A cidade ficava próxima à Base Naval de Sattahip e ao Aeródromo de U-Tapao, que abrigava bombardeiros B-52 da Força Aérea dos EUA.

Em 1966 e 1967, as tropas americanas representaram entre 11% e 16% de todos os visitantes da Tailândia .

Essa demanda impulsionou a abertura de hotéis, bares, casas noturnas e casas de massagem.

Uma lei de 1966 permitiu que estabelecimentos de entretenimento empregassem mulheres que oferecessem "serviços especiais". Isso criou uma zona cinzenta legal, embora a prostituição no país seja proibida desde 1960.

Quando as tropas americanas se retiraram em 1976, após o fim da Guerra do Vietnã, a infraestrutura permaneceu e facilitou a transição para o turismo civil em massa.

Enquanto isso, a Tailândia consolidava sua posição como destino turístico. O país teve um aumento expressivo no número de turistas nacionais e internacionais, passando de 200 mil em 1960 para 5 milhões em 1980.

Uma crise agrícola também impulsionou a migração de mulheres jovens das áreas rurais para as cidades, de acordo com o estudo da London School of Economics.

Na década de 1990, os distritos próximos às antigas bases militares americanas tinham cinco vezes mais profissionais do sexo do que aqueles próximos a bases não utilizadas pelos EUA.

Com o passar das décadas e o fim da Guerra Fria, a clientela de militares americanos foi amplamente substituída por viajantes europeus e, mais recentemente, por turistas russos e chineses.

Atualmente, segundo a agência Reuters, a indústria do sexo permanece abertamente visível na cidade, apesar de sua ilegalidade e das frequentes batidas policiais.

Enquanto isso, as autoridades locais tentam ampliar a imagem turística da cidade com ofertas de esportes, atividades familiares e bem-estar.

*Com informações de Jonathan Head, correspondente da BBC no Sudeste Asiático.

articles.title: Agricultor se emociona ao falar de incêndio em que perdeu tudo | G1
articles.standfirst: Francisco Rodrigues Sobrinho e a mulher conseguiram levar também os documentos. Incêndio atingiu, no total, uma área de cerca de mil hectares na zona rural de Santa Helena de Goiás e de outras cidades.
articles.summary: Francisco Rodrigues Sobrinho e a mulher conseguiram levar também os documentos. Incêndio atingiu, no total, uma área de cerca de mil hectares na zona rural de do sudoeste de Goiás.
articles.body:
Um agricultor perdeu a casa onde morava durante um incêndio que atingiu as lavouras da sua propriedade rural, em Santa Helena de Goiás , no sudoeste do estado. Em entrevista à TV Anhanguera, Francisco Rodrigues Sobrinho, que também é aposentado, chorou ao falar da destruição causada pelas chamas.

"É muito triste. Queimou foi tudo. Nós saímos só com a roupa do corpo e os documentos. Acabou tudo", lamentou.

Segundo apuração da TV Anhanguera, ele perdeu a lavoura e animais, além da casa em que morava com a esposa. A aposentada Maria Alves de Lima Rodrigues contou que todos os eletrodomésticos e móveis foram consumidos pelo fogo.

"Geladeira, freezer, forno elétrico, micro-ondas, batedeira, guarda-roupa, cama... mesa com as cadeiras. Foi tudo. Dois armários com as minhas compras dentro, com as compras que a gente faz para passar o mês", detalhou Maria.

O agricultor e aposentado Francisco Rodrigues Sobrinho perdeu a casa durante um incêndio na área rural de Santa Helena de Goiás — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

No total, o incêndio, que durou dois dias, atingiu uma área de cerca de mil hectares de lavouras e mato, abrangendo Maurilândia , Santa Helena, Rio Verde e o distrito de Lagoa do Bauzinho.

A chuva que caiu sobre a região sudoeste na quarta-feira (2) ajudou a apagar o incêndio, cujas chamas, em algumas áreas, chegaram a atingir dois metros de altura. Segundo o sargento do Corpo de Bombeiros Clenderson Rubens, o fogo estava se espalhando bem rápido, em função da velocidade do vento.

"A gente estava até com receio de que ele atravessasse uma rodovia porque ele atravessou alguns córregos que tinha na região", disse o sargento à TV Anhanguera.

De acordo com apuração da TV Anhanguera, a região que sofreu o incêndio segue sendo monitorada por bombeiros, brigadistas e produtores rurais em função do forte calor e ventania previstos para os próximos dias, condições favoráveis a novas queimadas.

articles.title: Terremoto de magnitude 5 atinge o Tibete, diz instituto alemão | G1
articles.standfirst: Primeiro abalo foi registrado a 10 km de profundidade; na semana passada, agências revisaram a causa de enchentes no Himalaia e concluíram que o desastre foi provocado pelo colapso de uma geleira, e não por um terremoto.
articles.summary: Abalo foi registrado a 10 km de profundidade; na semana passada, agências revisaram a causa de enchentes no Nepal e concluíram que o desastre foi provocado pelo colapso de uma gele
articles.body:
Epicentro de terremoto de magnitude 5.0 no Tibete registrado por agências sismológicas em 3 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/Google Maps

Um terremoto de magnitude 5 atingiu o Tibete , na China , nesta quinta-feira (3), informou o Centro Alemão de Pesquisa em Geociências ( GFZ ). Segundo o Serviço Geológico dos Estados Unidos ( USGS ), o epicentro do terremoto na região de Xizang, no oeste chinês, próximo à fronteira com a Índia .

Um segundo abalo, de magnitude 4.8 , foi registrado horas depois, às 8h39, na cidade chinesa de Mianyang. O município fica na região de Sichuan, também no planalto tibetano, no sudoeste do país, informou o Centro de Redes Sismológicas da China.

Segundo o instituto alemão, o primeiro tremor ocorreu a uma profundidade de 10 quilômetros . Até a última atualização desta reportagem, não havia informações sobre vítimas ou danos .

O abalo inicial atingiu a encosta de uma montanha na cordilheira no Himalaia às 2h16 pelo horário de Brasília. O terremoto desta quinta-feira (3) não fica próximo de onde ocorreram as enchentes da semana passada , na fronteira entre o Tibete e o Nepal .

O desastre iniciado na quarta-feira passada (26) deixou, ao menos, 1.252 mortes e 4.216 desaparecidos no Nepal. Do lado chinês, foram 21 vítimas fatais e 541 paradeiros .

Logo após o desabamento, especialistas notificaram que um lago formado após o colapso da geleira poderia se romper nos dias seguintes e provocar novas avalanches na região. O alerta foi divulgado pelo jornal Times of India, com base em informações de autoridades chinesas.

À época, agências de monitoramento sismológico chegaram a informar que as enchentes devastadoras no Nepal haviam sido desencadeadas por um terremoto. O USGS, por exemplo, registrou inicialmente um evento sísmico de magnitude 4,4 na região da fronteira entre s países atingidos.

Após uma análise mais detalhada de estações sísmicas, ondas de baixa frequência e imagens de satélite, porém, o órgão revisou a avaliação e afirmou que não houve abalo sísmico .

Segundo os pesquisadores, o sinal detectado pelos sismógrafos foi causado pelo colapso de uma geleira e pelo enorme fluxo de gelo, rochas e detritos que desceu montanha abaixo. O USGS atualizou o evento para uma magnitude equivalente a 5,2 e concluiu que a energia registrada foi produzida pelo deslizamento da massa de gelo, responsável pelas enchentes.

De acordo com especialistas, uma grande porção de geleira se desprendeu de uma encosta a cerca de 5.200 metros de altitude. A massa de gelo e rochas despencou pelo vale, atingiu um rio na região de Lhende Khola e gerou uma enxurrada carregada de detritos, que avançou rapidamente pelos cursos d'água até áreas habitadas.

articles.title: Putin nega nova mobilização de tropas para guerra na Ucrânia | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente russo rejeitou alerta feito pelo líder ucraniano e disse que não há necessidade de convocar mais reservistas para a guerra.
articles.summary: Presidente russo rejeitou alerta feito pelo líder ucraniano e disse que não há necessidade de convocar mais reservistas para a guerra.
articles.body:
O presidente da Rússia , Vladimir Putin , afirmou nesta quinta-feira (3) que o país não planeja uma nova mobilização de tropas para a guerra na Ucrânia e classificou como "desinformação" os rumores sobre uma possível convocação de reservistas.

"Até o momento, não há nenhum cenário que exija mobilização", disse Putin durante o Fórum Econômico Oriental, realizado em Vladivostok, no extremo leste da Rússia.

No começo de agosto, o presidente da Ucrânia , Volodimir Zelensky , afirmou ter recebido informações de inteligência indicando que Moscou preparava uma nova rodada de mobilização para o outono no Hemisfério Norte .

Putin rejeitou a informação e disse que se trata de uma tentativa de influenciar as eleições para a Duma, a Câmara Baixa do Parlamento russo, marcadas para ocorrer entre 18 e 20 de setembro.

"É um ataque de informação do inimigo às vésperas das eleições para a Duma", declarou.

Em setembro de 2022, a Rússia anunciou uma "mobilização parcial" de cerca de 300 mil reservistas para reforçar suas tropas na Ucrânia, meses após o início da invasão em larga escala do país vizinho.

A medida provocou a saída de milhares de russos do país. Desde então, o Kremlin tem evitado novas mobilizações, apesar das baixas registradas no campo de batalha .

articles.title: Frente fria se aproxima e faz chuvas terem data para voltar ao Paraná; veja previsão do tempo | G1
articles.standfirst: Semana começou com tempestades, passou a ter tempo firme, mas deve terminar com instabilidades. Informações são da Climatempo.
articles.summary: Semana começou com tempestades, passou a ter tempo firme, mas deve terminar com instabilidades. Informações são da Climatempo.
articles.body:
Após uma pequena trégua, as chuvas já têm data para voltar ao Paraná, segundo a Climatempo. A semana começou com tempestades e depois passou a ter tempo firme, mas deve terminar com instabilidades devido à aproximação de uma nova frente fria.

A previsão dos meteorologistas é que esta quinta-feira (3) ainda seja ensolarada em todo o estado, mas que o tempo mude já na sexta-feira (4), principalmente na metade sul paranaense. A Climatempo ainda afirma que no sábado (5) as chuvas se espalham e, no domingo (6), perdem força. Veja a previsão do tempo por região mais abaixo.

Veja, abaixo, o resumo da previsão estadual da Climatempo.

➡️A quinta-feira (3) será de tempo estável em todo o Paraná. A atuação de uma área de alta pressão e a presença de ar mais seco mantêm a ausência de chuva ao longo do dia. Enquanto isso, uma nova frente fria avança pelo extremo sul da Região Sul, ainda sem provocar mudança significativa nas condições do tempo em território paranaense. Durante a tarde, o aquecimento ganha força principalmente no oeste, noroeste e norte. Algumas áreas do interior e do leste paranaense devem contar com alerta para baixa umidade do ar durante a tarde.

➡️Na sexta-feira (4) , o tempo volta a mudar no Paraná. A frente fria que avança pela Região Sul alcança o estado e favorece o aumento da nebulosidade e o retorno da chuva. A instabilidade tende a ganhar espaço principalmente entre o sul, centro-sul, Região Metropolitana de Curitiba e áreas do leste, embora também alcance pontos mais para o interior. Antes do avanço mais efetivo do ar frio, as temperaturas ainda sobem bastante principalmente no norte e noroeste.

➡️No sábado (5) , a instabilidade aumenta de forma significativa no Paraná. A frente fria e o reforço do transporte de umidade favorecem chuva mais abrangente e volumes elevados, especialmente entre áreas do centro, centro-sul, Campos Gerais e leste. As temperaturas máximas diminuem em relação à sexta-feira.

➡️ No domingo (6) , a frente fria avança para outras áreas do país e a chuva tende a perder força no Paraná. Ainda assim, permanece instabilidade residual em partes do estado, enquanto uma área de alta pressão e o avanço de ar mais frio passam a determinar as condições meteorológicas. O resfriamento se intensifica e prepara um início de semana ainda mais frio, com aumento da condição para geada posteriormente.

articles.title: Grupo ajuda ex-simpatizantes de Trump a deixar o movimento MAGA | G1
articles.standfirst: Criada por um ex-ativista trumpista, a 'Leaving MAGA' acolhe quem se arrependeu de ter militado pelo movimento e busca romper com a desinformação, as teorias da conspiração e o extremismo que o cercam.
articles.summary: Criada por um ex-ativista trumpista, a 'Leaving MAGA' acolhe quem se arrependeu de ter militado pelo movimento e busca romper com a desinformação, as teorias da conspiração e o extremismo que o cercam.
articles.body:
Donald Trump responde a perguntas da imprensa durante evento no Salão Oval da Casa Branca, em 31 de agosto de 2026 — Foto: Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters

A organização funciona como um grupo de apoio a dependentes —no caso, do presidente Donald Trump e do movimento extremista que o sustenta. Criada em 2024, a “Leaving MAGA” (Rompendo com o MAGA) recebe e ajuda quem se arrependeu de ter se aliado a ele e quer se desvencilhar dos métodos violentos e radicais, das teorias de conspiração, da desinformação e da ideologia que cercam o movimento “Faça a América Grande Novamente”.

“O que eu diria hoje sobre mim é que me tornei um ser humano renascido”, resume o fundador do grupo, o escritor Rich Logis, autor de “One betrayal too many: why I left MAGA” ("Traições demais: porque eu deixei o MAGA", em português).

Logis conta que se tornou ativista e admirador fervoroso de Trump em 2015, após enxergar no magnata republicano o disruptor disposto e capaz de destruir a ordem política. Ele se engajou no MAGA, foi comentarista político na Fox News e no Federalist e participou das campanhas presidenciais em 2016 e 2020.

As decepções vieram com a gestão de Trump durante a pandemia da Covid e a invasão de simpatizantes do presidente ao Capitólio. Em agosto de 2022, conseguiu desligar-se do movimento.

“Foi preciso um ano de uma luta interna emocionalmente exaustiva antes que eu conseguisse deixar o movimento MAGA. Quando finalmente saí, em 30 de agosto de 2022, troquei o caos pela estabilidade. A decisão foi libertadora. Eu não precisava mais defender o indefensável nem justificar o injustificável”, escreveu ele no site da organização.

Em depoimentos, ex-integrantes do MAGA dizem ter sido doutrinados por influenciadores e radialistas de extrema direita , como Rush Limbaugh, Ben Shapiro e Tucker Carlson. Em comum, dizem não se arrepender apenas de terem votado em Trump, mas de terem militado por ele com entusiasmo, guiados pela desinformação.

Jennie Gage, do Arizona, lembra que via Trump como “um homem de família atendendo a um chamado por Deus para liderar o país”. Ela tinha certeza de que ele tinha se convertido ao cristianismo.

“O MAGA se tornou minha identidade por completo. Trump era a minha foto de perfil nas redes sociais. Eu postava declarações de amor por ele."

Paralelamente ao fanatismo pelo presidente, Jennie relata que se dava conta de que Trump aglutinava grupos com ideologias odiosas : mórmons, skinheads, batistas do Sul e evangélicos. “ Ele se tornou o Grande Mago de todos os grupos nacionalistas cristãos nos Estados Unidos . É a fusão político-religiosa definitiva”, conta.

A ficha começou a cair pela via da informação e de novas amizades, diz ela. Jennie leu livros sobre racismo, feminismo e gênero. “Minha visão do mundo anterior desmoronou. Percebi que a maior parte do que eu acreditava não era verdade. Há alguns anos, abandonei o cristianismo.”

Outdoor com mensagem de apoio para membros do movimento MAGA, que apoia o presidente Donald Trump, erguido pelo grupo 'Leaving MAGA' no estado de Washington, nos Estados Unidos, em agosto de 2026. — Foto: Divulgação/Leaving MAGA

Para Belle Sarnes, que cresceu em uma comunidade mórmon em Utah, o rompimento com o MAGA veio com a participação de Trump nos arquivos do criminoso sexual Jeffrey Epstein e com a campanha de deportação em massa promovida no segundo mandato.

“Sinto vergonha e remorso por ter sido tão ingênua, a ponto de acreditar que imigrantes ilegais estavam dominando os EUA, que essas pessoas estavam levando nossos impostos e vivendo às custas do país. Eles estão simplesmente visando qualquer pessoa de pele morena. É um Holocausto moderno. Devastador, para dizer o mínimo.”

Rich Logis, o fundador da “Leaving MAGA”, acredita que sem uma comunidade para integrá-los, é mais difícil para os céticos abandonarem o movimento. Nesse processo de desintoxicação da ideologia radical, a entidade facilita, por meio do grupo Solutions and Serenity, encontros para ajudar parentes a interagir com pessoas que foram afetadas pelo MAGA.

Outra ação da “Leaving MAGA” é a campanha de outdoors em 20 estados dos EUA com uma mensagem direta, dirigida aos filiados que questionam suas convicções e buscam abandonar o extremismo do movimento. “Tem dúvidas? Você não está sozinho.”

articles.title: Porta-aviões dos EUA que atracou na Tailândia após missão de quase 300 dias viraliza por aparentar desgaste; veja VÍDEO e FOTOS | G1
articles.standfirst: USS Abraham Lincoln, que participou da guerra contra o Irã no Oriente Médio desde fevereiro, chegou nesta semana a porto tailandês e apresentou casco escurecido.
articles.summary: USS Abraham Lincoln, que participou da guerra contra o Irã no Oriente Médio desde fevereiro, chegou nesta semana a porto tailandês e apresentou casco escurecido.
articles.body:
Uma cena incomum envolvendo o Exército dos Estados Unidos chamou a atenção do público e viralizou nas redes sociais nesta semana. O porta-aviões USS Abraham Lincoln chegou à Tailândia com diversas manchas no casco, e as fotos do navio rapidamente renderam milhões de visualizações.

A embarcação atracou na quarta-feira no porto de Laem Chabang para manutenção, e seus cinco mil marinheiros desceram ficarão hospedados em Pattaya, conhecida como a "cidade do pecado" , no local após passarem quase 300 dias em alto mar.

O USS Abraham Lincoln deixou os EUA em novembro de 2025 e em janeiro foi enviado para o Oriente Médio. Após meses participando da guerra contra o Irã, ele foi trocado pelo USS George Washington após denúncias de crise de saúde mental entre os marinheiros por conta do longo destacamento, incluindo relatos de tentativas de suicídio.

articles.title: Três são condenados por fraude ao criar hectares fictícios no TO | G1
articles.standfirst: A fraude de terras em Paranã envolveu uma ex-oficiala de cartório e dois irmãos que movimentaram mais de R$ 5 milhões com documentos falsos.
articles.summary: A fraude de terras em Paranã envolveu uma ex-oficiala de cartório e dois irmãos que movimentaram mais de R$ 5 milhões com documentos falsos.
articles.body:
Cidade de Paranã (TO) — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Paranã

Dois irmãos e uma ex-oficiala do Cartório de Imóveis de Paranã foram condenados por falsificar documentos públicos ao criar mais de 5 mil hectares fictícios no município. O crime aconteceu entre 2006 e junho de 2013. Conforme a Justiça, os réus chegaram a emitir 11 certidões falsas, a partir de um imóvel de 310 hectares.

A sentença foi expedida pelo juiz Frederico Paiva Bandeira de Souza, da 1ª Escrivania Criminal de Paranã. Segundo o documento, Ricardo Neves Prudente atuava como articulador das fraudes, Rafael Neves Prudente na intermediação e venda das áreas, e Maíra Nunes Paula trabalhava como oficiala do Cartório de Paranã na época.

O g1 solicitou um posicionamento às defesas dos réus, mas não teve resposta até a última atualização da reportagem.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

No esquema, eram emitidas certidões falsas de imóveis rurais e forjadas as datas para parecer que os documentos haviam sido lavrados em 1990 e 1995. Segundo a Justiça, os réus ainda usaram o nome de um homem falecido em 1965 para transferir os imóveis para a empresa de fachada do grupo.

As terras eram divididas em parcelas inferiores a 500 hectares, para tentar dispensar a obrigatoriedade do georreferenciamento para a emissão do Certificado de Cadastro de Imóvel Rural. O grupo também atuava na negociação de propina a servidores públicos para tentar destravar o registro das áreas fictícias em órgãos ambientais e agrários.

Investigações do Grupo de Atuação Especial de Combate ao Crime Organizado (Gaeco) também apontaram que os réus movimentaram valores milionários, superiores ao que declaravam. Somadas as contas bancárias dos três, somente no ano de 2013, a movimentação financeira total foi de R$ 5.008.625,16.

Os réus foram condenados a cinco anos e 10 meses de prisão e devem cumprir a pena em regime semiaberto.

articles.title: Cabo Frio volta a receber voos de Belo Horizonte na alta temporada | G1
articles.standfirst: Operação da Azul começa em dezembro e terá voos até fevereiro de 2027; as passagens já estão à venda.
articles.summary: Operação da Azul começa em dezembro e terá voos até fevereiro de 2027; as passagens já estão à venda.
articles.body:
Cabo Frio retoma vôos diretos de Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais — Foto: Prefeitura de Cabo Frio

O Aeroporto Internacional de Cabo Frio , na Região dos Lagos do Rio, voltará a receber voos diretos de Belo Horizonte , Minas Gerais, durante a próxima alta temporada. A operação da Azul começa em 12 de dezembro de 2026 e segue até 27 de fevereiro de 2027. As passagens já estão à venda.

A frequência dos voos vai mudar ao longo da temporada. Entre 12 e 26 de dezembro, as viagens serão realizadas às terças, quartas, sextas e sábados. Já entre 28 de dezembro e 3 de janeiro, período que inclui o réveillon, haverá voos todos os dias.

Depois desse período, a operação volta a ter quatro frequências semanais. Entre 5 de janeiro e 27 de fevereiro de 2027, os voos de Belo Horizonte para Cabo Frio estarão disponíveis às terças, quartas, sextas e sábados.

Segundo a Prefeitura de Cabo Frio, a retomada da ligação direta com Belo Horizonte atende a uma demanda de turistas e amplia as opções de acesso à cidade e aos demais municípios da Região dos Lagos durante o período de maior movimento turístico.

A retomada ocorre no mesmo período em que Cabo Frio terá novamente voos comerciais regulares de Guarulhos, em São Paulo. No início de agosto, a Latam anunciou quatro voos semanais para a cidade a partir de dezembro, às segundas, quintas, sextas e domingos.

A operação da Latam também marcará a chegada do Embraer E195-E2 a Cabo Frio. A rota entre Cabo Frio e Guarulhos está entre quatro novas ligações incluídas nas 42 rotas que serão operadas pela companhia com o modelo a partir de novembro.

A alteração faz parte de um novo sistema binário implantado pela Prefeitura de Belém, que também envolve a rua Municipalidade. A proposta é reorganizar o fluxo de veículos e reduzir os pontos de retenção na região.

Com o novo esquema, a Pedro Álvares Cabral passa a concentrar o fluxo no sentido bairro-centro. Já a rua Municipalidade recebe parte dos veículos que antes utilizavam a Pedro Álvares Cabral no sentido contrário.

Segundo a Prefeitura, a mudança ocorre após a conclusão das obras de requalificação da Municipalidade. O sistema binário transforma vias próximas e paralelas, que anteriormente tinham circulação nos dois sentidos, em ruas de sentido único e direções opostas.

Além da mudança no sentido das vias, a intervenção inclui 1,7 quilômetro de nova ciclofaixa e outros 1,7 quilômetro de faixa azul, espaço destinado à circulação preferencial de motociclistas.

articles.title: Pakistan’s Punjab allows ‘secret’ terrorism trials: Why it’s controversial
articles.summary: A single unnamed official can order anonymous judges, prosecutors and witnesses in terrorism cases, with no time limit.
articles.body:
Islamabad, Pakistan — Politicians in Punjab, Pakistan’s most populous province, have passed a law allowing terrorism trials to be held in near-total secrecy, with the judge, prosecutor and witnesses permitted to remain anonymous.

Under the law, a person facing the country’s most serious criminal charge could be convicted without learning who heard the case against them, who prosecuted it or who testified.

The trial record can be sealed, and an appeal could be heard by judges never told who presided over the original trial.

The Anti-Terrorism (Punjab Amendment) Bill 2026 passed the Punjab Assembly on August 31, after opposition politicians staged a walkout in protest.

Four days earlier, the government had appeared to relent, agreeing to have the bill reviewed by the law department or a parliamentary committee.

When it returned to the floor, it was unchanged and passed without amendment on Monday.

The law has drawn criticism from opposition politicians, lawyers, rights groups and analysts, who say it concentrates enormous power in a single, unnamed official and could be used against government critics.

The law lets the government appoint a senior bureaucrat as a “designated authority” tasked with deciding what cases are to be heard under the special provisions earmarked in the legislation.

The official’s identity is kept confidential, known only to the chief justice of the Lahore High Court.

The official can declare any terrorism case, or even a whole category of them, a “special security case” if they conclude that the people involved need special “protection”.

The law does not clearly define the parameters that need to be met, and the accused cannot contest being placed under this category. Once the official requests it, the chief justice assigns the case to a sitting anti-terrorism court judge. A panel of five public prosecutors is drawn up, and the official picks one.

From there, the identities of the judge, prosecutor, police officers, witnesses and defence lawyers cannot be disclosed under any circumstances. Official titles are used instead of names, and court orders are signed without revealing who signed them.

Witnesses are identified only by codes. Hearings can be held over videolink, including from inside a prison, with voice-altering technology used to disguise participants.

The case file is sealed and held jointly by the chief justice and the official.

The law includes no expiry date, and a final clause allows the government to adopt “such other measures as it may deem appropriate”, leaving room to add further powers without further legislation.

Why is the government doing this, and why now?

The government’s official justification, laid out in the bill itself, points to increased cases of attacks by armed groups, and rising threats faced by judges, prosecutors, investigators and witnesses. It argues that the existing law does not adequately protect them.

Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan, on the floor of the assembly, invoked Pakistan’s toll from terrorism over the past two decades to argue that the assembly was the right forum to strengthen prosecutions.

Khalid Mahmood Ranjha, the legislator who tabled the bill, told Al Jazeera that the chief justice, not the designated authority, nominates the trial judge.

“There is no interference of the executive,” he said.

He dismissed fears that the law could be used against political opponents.

“It is just an apprehension,” the politician said, calling the criticism “propaganda to politicise and make the law controversial”.

“This law [is] only for hardened terrorists.”

But no single attack or case has been publicly named as the trigger.

Punjab also records only a small share of Pakistan’s terrorism-related deaths each year.

The vast majority occur in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, which together account for more than 90 percent of the country’s terrorism deaths.

Al Jazeera contacted Azma Bokhari, Punjab’s provincial minister for information, Marriyum Aurangzeb, senior minister in the Punjab government, and Rana Muhammad Iqbal, Punjab’s law minister, but did not receive a response.

Rida Hosain, a Lahore-based constitutional lawyer, said the threats facing judges, prosecutors and witnesses in Pakistan are real.

“There is no denying that Pakistan’s people and land have paid a devastating price for terrorism,” she told Al Jazeera. But she said no one who has actually read the amendment “can reasonably claim that it is consistent with due process”.

Opposition politicians argued the law violates the constitutional right to a fair trial and hands judicial-style powers to an unelected official with no oversight.

Ahmer Rasheed Bhatti, the independent legislator affiliated with jailed opposition leader Imran Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaaf (PTI) party, led objections on the floor.

“It creates a parallel procedure in which the executive, not the court, decides what a fair trial will look like,” he told Al Jazeera.

The designated authority must consult the chief justice, he said, but does not need their agreement.

Hosain said the secrecy itself removes a basic safeguard.

“By introducing faceless courts, an accused is deprived of the ability to challenge judicial bias and safeguard judicial impartiality,” she told Al Jazeera. “While this law remains in force, the right to a fair trial and due process is effectively suspended in Punjab.”

The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) also raised the alarm.

“The bill does not adequately define the circumstances in which these extraordinary powers may be invoked,” the commission’s spokesperson told Al Jazeera.

That, HRCP said, creates scope for abuse against ordinary citizens, political opponents or protesters in the name of security.

Mian Dawood, a Lahore-based constitutional lawyer, said existing law already lets courts protect witnesses and hold closed hearings under a judge’s control.

The new law, he said, moves that control to the executive rather than filling a gap. He said someone wrongly caught up in the system would have little recourse. Remedies such as a malicious-prosecution claim exist on paper but are “impracticable” in Pakistan’s courts, he said.

“A citizen has to suffer the misuse of powers by the state authorities,” the constitutional expert said.

Majid Nizami, a Lahore-based analyst, told Al Jazeera that Punjab province’s original antiterrorism law — enacted in 1997 and now amended with the controversial new provisions — was also misused.

“It looked very good on paper too,” Nizami said. “But what happened, eventually, was that it was used for political point-scoring and political manoeuvring.”

He said the law has, since 1997, been applied against nearly every major political party in Pakistan.

Nizami said he could not identify a Punjab case in the past decade where witness intimidation had derailed a prosecution — the ostensible justification for shielding the privacy of prosecutors and judges under the new amendments.

But there are older precedents. One case that stands out involved rebel commander Malik Ishaq. Ishaq co-founded Lashkar-e-Jhangvi, a sectarian group blamed for killing hundreds of people, most of them Shia Muslims.

Named in more than 200 criminal cases, he repeatedly walked free after witnesses and even judges grew too frightened to move against him, until he was killed in a 2015 shootout after armed men freed him from police custody.

Punjab itself passed a law last year giving authorities the power to detain terrorism suspects for up to three months without charge, part of a wider wave in which Balochistan and the federal government passed near-identical detention powers in 2025.

Balochistan passed a similar law in September 2025, letting a senior official anonymously flag cases for the same kind of concealed proceedings. It has been in force for about a year, without any publicly known case of its use.

Ranjha told Al Jazeera that Balochistan and Sindh had “already passed this law,” and that Punjab needed to follow.

While Sindh has amended its own antiterrorism law, it is only to let the provincial government resize or abolish antiterrorism courts based on caseload. It introduces no comparable anonymity or secrecy provisions. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has not amended its law along either track.

Salman Ghani, a political analyst, said Punjab’s situation differs from Balochistan’s for a simpler reason. “Punjab is still governable, and we don’t see terrorism incidents here every other day,” he told Al Jazeera.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which, alongside Balochistan, faces the overwhelming majority of the country’s terrorism violence, has not adopted secret trials; Punjab, which faces almost none of it, has.

“The federal government looks instrumental,” Bhatti told Al Jazeera. “Provinces appear to have been asked to enact similar amendments.”

He does not believe Punjab’s government developed that appetite on its own. “You are not looking at a local caseload,” he said. “You are looking at a request.”

Opposition politicians have argued that the law conflicts with the constitution’s fair-trial guarantees and oversteps what a provincial assembly can legislate, since antiterrorism law falls under federal jurisdiction.

With no sunset clause built in, the law does not expire on its own; whether it survives will most likely be decided in court rather than by the assembly that passed it.

Bhatti drew a comparison with the last time Pakistan departed this far from ordinary courts: military trials for civilians, introduced only through a constitutional amendment after the 2014 Peshawar Army Public School massacre, and built with a two-year limit unless parliament renewed it.

“You do not need a faceless provincial trial in the safer province,” he told Al Jazeera, “Unless the facelessness is the point.”

articles.title: Jackie Chan became the face of a campaign to save one of the world's most trafficked mammals; his Kung Fu Pangolin campaign urged China to stop buying their scales
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Jackie Chan, one of China's best-known film stars, became the face of a high-profile campaign in 2017 aimed at reducing demand for pangolin products a.
articles.body: Jackie Chan, one of China's best-known film stars, became the face of a high-profile campaign in 2017 aimed at reducing demand for pangolin products and helping protect one of the world's most trafficked mammals. The campaign, called “Kung Fu Pangolin”, used Chan's martial-arts image to deliver a simple message to consumers in China and Vietnam, where pangolin meat and scales had been in demand. In the 47-second public-service advertisement, Chan tries to teach pangolins kung fu so they can defend themselves against poachers, only to discover that the animals respond to danger by curling into protective balls. Produced by WildAid with The Nature Conservancy, the campaign urged people not to buy pangolin products and highlighted how consumer demand can fuel the illegal wildlife trade.Jackie Chan took on a new fight to save pangolinsJackie Chan's role in the campaign was to use his enormous popularity to bring attention to an animal that was far less familiar to the public than tigers, elephants or rhinos. In the “Kung Fu Pangolin” advertisement, the martial-arts star attempts to train pangolins to defend themselves against poachers, but the animals repeatedly curl into balls when threatened. The humorous idea was built around a serious fact about pangolins. Their natural defence against predators is to roll themselves into a tight ball, but this offers little protection when humans can simply pick them up and transport them. The campaign was created by WildAid and The Nature Conservancy, with the China Wildlife Conservation Association also involved, and was designed to discourage consumers from buying pangolin meat and scales. Chan's celebrity status gave the campaign access to a mass audience and helped turn pangolin trafficking into a more visible public issue.Why pangolins became one of the world's most trafficked mammalsPangolins have been heavily targeted by illegal wildlife traders because of demand for their meat and scales. Their scales are made of keratin, the same protein found in human fingernails and hair, but they have historically been used in traditional medicine based on claims that are not supported by modern scientific evidence. Pangolin meat has also been consumed as food in some markets. The combination of these demands has made pangolins a valuable target for poachers and traffickers. All eight pangolin species are threatened, although their individual conservation classifications vary, with some listed as Critically Endangered and others as Endangered or Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List. The animals are particularly vulnerable to hunting because they are slow-moving and rely on curling into a ball rather than fleeing when confronted. Once captured, they can be transported relatively easily, making them attractive targets for illegal wildlife traders.The scale of the trade prompted international action. At the 2016 Conference of the Parties to CITES, all eight pangolin species were transferred to Appendix I, the convention's highest level of protection. The listing, which took effect in January 2017, prohibited international commercial trade in wild pangolins and their parts. However, the measure did not automatically eliminate illegal trafficking or domestic markets, making demand reduction an important part of the wider conservation response.How the Kung Fu Pangolin campaign reached ChinaWildAid did not rely only on the online video featuring Chan. The organisation distributed the campaign through a large outdoor advertising network in China, placing the message on more than 100,000 screens across 37 cities. Billboards and other public advertisements were also used to reinforce the campaign. WildAid reported that the campaign's social-media content generated millions of views, while donated media support helped extend its reach across major population centres. The strategy was designed to put pangolin conservation in front of ordinary consumers rather than limiting the message to wildlife enthusiasts.The campaign was part of WildAid's broader effort to reduce demand for wildlife products in China and Vietnam. Its philosophy was that stopping illegal wildlife trafficking requires more than catching poachers and intercepting shipments. If consumers continue to purchase products made from threatened animals, there remains a financial incentive to capture and transport them. WildAid therefore sought to make wildlife consumption socially undesirable while explaining the consequences for endangered species. Chan's involvement was especially useful because the campaign could use humour and his martial-arts persona to communicate the message without relying on technical conservation language.Did Jackie Chan's campaign change attitudes towards pangolin products?There were indications that demand-reduction campaigns were changing public perceptions, although the available evidence does not prove that the Jackie Chan advertisement alone reduced the illegal pangolin trade. WildAid reported that the proportion of surveyed Chinese respondents who believed pangolin scales had medicinal value fell from 70% in 2015 to 50% in 2017, around the period when its pangolin demand-reduction campaign was being conducted. The organisation also commissioned research into reactions to the Jackie Chan advertisement, with respondents reporting that the PSA made them less likely to purchase pangolin products. These findings are useful evidence of changing attitudes, but they measure perceptions and self-reported intentions rather than actual purchases or trafficking volumes.That distinction is important when assessing celebrity conservation campaigns. A successful advertisement can raise awareness and make consumers reconsider their behaviour, but it cannot by itself stop poaching networks or guarantee that wildlife products disappear from illegal markets. Pangolin conservation requires enforcement, habitat protection, international cooperation and long-term reductions in consumer demand. Chan's contribution was therefore primarily in communication and public engagement rather than direct wildlife protection.China strengthened pangolin protection after the campaignThe campaign formed part of a broader period of change in pangolin conservation. China strengthened its domestic protection of pangolins in 2020, when all pangolin species in the country were upgraded from second-class to first-class nationally protected wild animals. The move provided the animals with stronger legal protection and reflected growing concern over their conservation status and illegal exploitation. China also introduced additional measures aimed at restricting the use and trade of pangolin products.The international and domestic measures complemented campaigns aimed at changing consumer behaviour. CITES restrictions addressed international commercial trade, Chinese law strengthened domestic protection, and organisations such as WildAid worked to reduce demand. Together, these approaches recognised that trafficking cannot be addressed effectively through enforcement alone if there is still a market for the products.Pangolins, meanwhile, remain under pressure despite these interventions. Illegal trafficking continues to pose a major threat, and seizures of pangolin scales have been reported in different parts of the world even after international trade restrictions were strengthened. Conservationists therefore continue to emphasise the need for enforcement, protection of wild populations and sustained efforts to discourage people from buying pangolin products. Chan's campaign did not end the trade, but it helped bring the issue to a much larger audience.The lasting significance of “Kung Fu Pangolin” is the way it turned a complicated wildlife-trafficking problem into an easily understood message. Jackie Chan did not single-handedly save the pangolin, nor can the campaign be credited with ending the illegal trade. Its value was in using one of China's most recognisable celebrities to challenge the perceived value of pangolin products and connect consumer choices with the survival of a threatened group of mammals. The campaign showed how celebrity influence can complement scientific research, international agreements and government enforcement by tackling another critical part of the problem, the demand that keeps illegal wildlife markets profitable.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Now is the time for action': UN warns of climate risks, says 1.5°C breach likely within years
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Global temperatures are likely to cross the 1.5-degree Celsius threshold within the next few years, intensifying extreme weather, ecosystem loss and t.
articles.body: Global temperatures are likely to cross the 1.5-degree Celsius threshold within the next few years, intensifying extreme weather, ecosystem loss and the risks facing small island developing states and low-lying coastal cities, according to a new UN report released on Wednesday.The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) report, titled Limiting Overshoot, stressed the need for immediate and sustained cuts in greenhouse gas emissions to limit the duration and magnitude of warming beyond the 1.5°C threshold.“It is still possible to bring temperatures down and achieve global goals in the Paris Agreement,” the report said.However, it also warned that above 1.5°C, climate risks and impacts would intensify with every additional fraction of a degree and each passing year. The expected consequences include more intense extreme weather, ecosystem loss and the submersion of small island developing states and low-lying coastal cities.Guterres calls for ‘overshoot of ambition’UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said recent extreme weather events were a warning of what could lie ahead.“This summer's scorching heat, raging wildfires and deadly floods are a warning of what lies ahead. We must make the overshoot above 1.5 degrees as small and short as possible. That demands an overshoot of ambition,” Guterres said.The report called for immediate and sustained reductions in greenhouse gas emissions, including methane, to minimise peak warming on the path to net-zero emissions.UNEP Executive Director Inger Andersen said governments must intensify climate action by cutting emissions, strengthening resilience and adaptation, and ensuring that any exceedance of 1.5°C is as small and short as possible.“Now is the time we must double down on climate action. We can — and must — get on the right path,” Andersen said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Iran Red Crescent urges ICC probe into deadly US strike on wedding party
articles.summary: Outrage grows over US strike that killed four people and wounded 67 at a wedding party in Kuhestak.
articles.body:
The Iranian Red Crescent Society has asked the International Criminal Court (ICC) to investigate a missile attack by the United States that hit a wedding party in the southern town of Kuhestak, killing at least four people and wounding dozens.

In a letter to the court on Wednesday, the humanitarian group said the attack warrants “an independent, impartial, thorough, and effective investigation” given the “civilian character of the location”.

The strike, which took place at 9:30pm local time (18:00 GMT) on Tuesday, killed at least four people and wounded 67, the group said, warning that the number of deaths may increase “given the critical condition of some of the injured”.

Those killed were two women and two children, aged four and 16. An Iranian official said most of the wounded were also women and children.

The Red Crescent said the attack could amount to a “war crime”, noting that international law prohibits directing attacks against civilians or civilian objects, or launching a strike while knowing it could cause disproportionate civilian harm.

The US Central Command said it was aware of the reports about the attack in Iranian media, but said it does not target civilians.

Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs rejected the claim, with spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei citing past US strikes on civilians in Iraq and Afghanistan. He noted on X that such attacks have also been portrayed in US television shows.

“The reality is so horrifying that even American propaganda has never dared make the claim [the CENTCOM] is making today,” he wrote. “Sirik is not a story. The civilians are real. The victims are real.”

Neither the US nor Iran are party to the ICC’s Rome Statute, meaning the court does not have automatic jurisdiction over either nation.

But Dawn, a human rights group, has previously said Iran could still accept the court’s ad hoc jurisdiction over crimes committed on its territory from a specific date. “By filing such a declaration, set to the beginning of the war, Iran would grant the ICC jurisdiction over every strike on Iranian soil,” the group said.

The strike in Kuhestak came as the US launched a wave of attacks on Iranian coastal areas near the blockaded Strait of Hormuz, accusing Tehran of attempting to launch strikes against US troops and commercial shipping in the waterway.

Iran’s Ministry of Health said at least 18 people were killed in Tuesday’s strikes, while 142 were wounded.

Iran’s envoy to the United Nations, Gholamhossein Darzi, called on the UN Security Council to denounce the Kuhestak attack.

“The Islamic Republic strongly condemns this horrific and appalling crime,” he wrote, adding that “the deliberate targeting and killing of civilians, including children, constitutes a grave violation of the fundamental rules of international humanitarian law and amounts to a war crime.”

Iranian authorities say at least 3,468 people were killed in the initial phase of the US and Israel’s war, which began on February 28 and ended with a ceasefire on April 8. A second round of hostilities, from July 27 to August 24, killed a further 59 people and wounded 666.

The deadliest single attack of the war, in terms of civilian casualties, destroyed an elementary school in Minab on the war’s first day. At least 156 people, including 120 children, were killed. A separate strike that day hit a sports hall in Lamerd, killing 21 people, including four children.

Over more than six months of war, the US and Israel have also struck oil and gas facilities, fuel depots, steel and petrochemical factories, airports, ports, bridges, power installations, medical centres and water facilities across Iran.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Jacques Kallis: "I realised in Sri Lanka that my dream of playing in a World Cup was..."
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Two athletes can reach the same realisation, that a long-held goal is no longer realistically within reach- and handle that moment in very different w.
articles.body: Two athletes can reach the same realisation, that a long-held goal is no longer realistically within reach- and handle that moment in very different ways. One keeps chasing the goal anyway, past the point where the numbers and the body have stopped supporting it, unwilling to let go of something they've built an identity around. The other names the gap plainly, admits the goal has moved out of reach, and adjusts their remaining career around that honest assessment instead of around denial. Kallis, widely regarded as one of the finest all-round cricketers in the sport's history, made this exact admission in 2014, timing his retirement from one-day and T20 cricket around the specific, concrete moment he recognised that another World Cup campaign simply wasn't realistic for him anymore, rather than continuing to chase a milestone the calendar had already ruled out.Quote of the day by Jacques Kallis"I realised in Sri Lanka that my dream of playing in a World Cup was a bridge too far."Written at the end of a career defined partly by near-missesWhat gives this line its particular weight is the shape of Kallis's career around the tournament he's referring to. Across nearly two decades playing for South Africa, from his Test debut in 1995 through his retirement from limited-overs cricket in 2014, Kallis established himself as one of the most complete players the game has produced, a genuine all-rounder capable of anchoring an innings with the bat, taking key wickets with the ball, and holding some of the safest hands in the slips. Despite that individual excellence, a Cricket World Cup title remained out of reach for both Kallis personally and for South Africa as a team throughout his career, a national side that developed a reputation for falling agonisingly short in major tournaments across multiple World Cup campaigns during exactly the years Kallis was playing.The Guardian reported his announcement in July 2014, in which Kallis explained that a trip to Sri Lanka had been the moment the reality became unavoidable: another World Cup, specifically the 2015 tournament, was no longer a realistic target given his age and the physical toll of continued international cricket. Rather than dragging the decision out or attempting one more campaign against those odds, he retired from the shorter formats at that point, closing the door on the one major honour that had eluded him across an otherwise decorated career.A simple way to actually use this ideaThe useful move here is treating an honest recalculation of what's still realistically achievable as a legitimate part of pursuing any long-term goal, rather than as a form of giving up. Continuing to chase a target well past the point where the odds have genuinely shifted against it isn't automatically persistence; sometimes it's simply a refusal to update an assessment that circumstances have already changed.A fair test, when a long-held goal starts to look increasingly unlikely, is to ask honestly whether the remaining effort would be better spent finishing well on different terms, rather than continuing to chase a version of success that the situation no longer supports. That question won't make giving up a specific target feel painless. It usually makes the decision, once made, a clean one rather than a slow, reluctant fade.Other quotes by Jacques Kallis"Retiring from cricket is not about form. I feel that the time is now and it's right. I've tried to give everything I have when I've played the game, the game goes on." "I am excited about it. No-one really knows him [Kumar Sangakkara] as a person and everyone is looking forward to that." "We should not play like Australia or India or England - we should play like Sri Lanka."Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Ex-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and wife seek to end drug charges case on immunity grounds
articles.summary: Maduro and his wife asked a judge on Wednesday to dismiss the drug trafficking indictment against them on the grounds that they have immunity as the leader and first lady of a foreign country.
articles.body: NEW YORK — Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife asked a judge on Wednesday to dismiss the drug trafficking indictment against them on the grounds that they have immunity as the leader and first lady of a foreign country. In papers filed in Manhattan federal court, lawyers for Maduro said a judge was required by law to reject the indictment because it cannot be brought against a foreign leader. “No American court has ever presided over the criminal trial of a foreign leader who was recognized by their own country as the sitting head of state at the time the charges were brought,” the lawyers wrote. “That is not an accident of history. It reflects a rule older than the common law: heads of state are exempt from the criminal process of any national court but their own.” Maduro and his wife are scheduled to go on trial on drug trafficking charges next June 1. Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein has set oral arguments for Nov. 17 on motions to dismiss the indictment. Maduro, 63, and his wife, Cilia Flores, 69, have been held at a Brooklyn jail since U.S. forces seized them from their Caracas home in a middle-of-the-night raid in early January and brought them to New York. In separate papers filed Wednesday, lawyers for Flores said she too has immunity from U.S. prosecution on sovereign immunity grounds. “It is an attribute of Venezuela’s sovereignty, and only Venezuela may surrender it,” her lawyers wrote. Maduro’s lawyers said that even if Maduro were not entitled to sovereign immunity as the head of state, the case against him must be dismissed because he is also entitled to conduct-based sovereign immunity. Meanwhile, the lawyers argued, Maduro “vehemently denies the allegations against him.” “If this case were to proceed to trial, it would be apparent that he has been falsely accused,” they said. Both have pleaded not guilty in a criminal case first brought six years ago against numerous alleged co-conspirators. They face potential life prison sentences if a jury agrees that they were part of a conspiracy to send cocaine into the U.S. Federal prosecutors are scheduled to file a response to the arguments later this month. President Donald Trump’s administration has defended the raid to capture Maduro as a “surgical law enforcement operation.” Maduro has called himself a prisoner of war and his capture a kidnapping. U.S. prosecutors say Maduro carried out a conspiracy to move thousands of tons of cocaine into the U.S. by colluding with Venezuelan law enforcement to help drug kingpins.
