articles.title: India unveils 10-year ‘RAKSHA’ roadmap to expand global defence & security ties
articles.summary: News News: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Thursday released the ‘RAKSHA’ document on defence diplomacy, outlining India's strategic roadmap and vision for exp.
articles.body: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Thursday released the ‘RAKSHA’ document on defence diplomacy, outlining India's strategic roadmap and vision for expanding global defence partnerships over the next 10 years.The document, unveiled at a special event in New Delhi, lays out a framework aimed at aligning India's national security objectives with proactive international cooperation, according to the ministry of defence.The strategic blueprint focuses on deepening bilateral and multilateral security ties, building capacity with friendly countries, promoting indigenous defence exports and strengthening maritime security.Four key pillars of India's defence diplomacy roadmapThe ‘RAKSHA’ framework is built around four key pillars:Strategic partnerships: Deepening bilateral and multilateral security cooperation.Capacity building: Expanding joint military exercises, training programmes and the sharing of best practices with friendly nations.Indigenous exports: Promoting Make-in-India defence platforms to position India as a reliable global defence manufacturing hub.Maritime security: Strengthening India's role as a Net Security Provider and First Responder in the Indian Ocean Region.The ministry of defence said the document provides a “clear, actionable vision” for the next decade as defence diplomacy remains a core pillar of India's foreign policy.The framework is aimed at ensuring India remains an anchor of peace, stability and a rules-based order in an evolving global landscape.Senior officials attend release eventChief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth, defence secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh and secretary (defence production) Sanjeev Kumar were among the senior officials present at the event.Secretary (east) in the ministry of external affairs Rudrendra Tandon, Vice Chief of the Air Staff Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit and Vice Chief of the Naval Staff Vice Admiral Ajay Kochhar also attended.The document was officially released during an event at Kartavya Bhawan.The directorate of public relations, ministry of defence, said in a post on X that the framework sets a 10-year roadmap to strengthen global security partnerships.“Aligning national security with proactive international cooperation, this comprehensive framework aims to position India as a key defence manufacturing hub and an anchor of regional stability,” it added.The document also seeks to strengthen India's role as a Net Security Provider and First Responder in the Indian Ocean Region, with defence diplomacy described as a core pillar of the country's foreign policy.Rajnath Singh calls for stronger India-Belgium cooperationThe release came a day after India and Belgium held extensive discussions aimed at expanding bilateral defence and industrial cooperation.Singh hosted Belgian defence and trade minister Theo Francken in New Delhi on Wednesday, with multiple memorandums of understanding and contracts signed under defence industrial cooperation.“Had a very productive meeting with the Defence and Trade Minister of Belgium, Mr @FranckenTheo, in New Delhi today. We reviewed the entire spectrum of Defence relations and Defence Industrial Cooperation between India and Belgium. Multiple MoUs and contracts under the Defence Industrial Cooperation were also signed, towards leveraging Belgian technology together with Indian skill and scale,” Singh said.On Thursday, Singh called for greater cooperation between the two countries during the India-Belgium Ministers' Meeting in the national capital.“The world is witnessing a time of great geopolitical and economic turmoil. Most of it is not our doing, but we have to handle the challenges. In such situations, meeting a friend and partner like you provides a useful opportunity to exchange views and perspectives,” he said.Singh said the recently held India-Belgium Strategic Dialogue had provided a framework for taking the bilateral partnership forward, including in defence and security.

articles.title: Russia’s strikes near Moldova raise alarm over Putin’s plans for Europe’s eastern flank
articles.summary: President Sandu's national security advisor, Stanislav Secrieru, says Russia's strikes on Ukrainian-Moldovan border infrastructure aim to sever vital grain export corridors to European markets.
articles.body: As the war in neighboring Ukraine moves closer to its border, the former Soviet republic of Moldova, which just marked 35 years of independence, faces growing pressure from Russia. In exclusive comments to Fox News Digital, national security advisor to Moldova’s President Maia Sandu, Stanislav Secrieru, said Russia’s recent strikes against Ukrainian-Moldovan border infrastructure pose a major threat to Ukraine’s economy and access to European markets. Secrieru told Fox News Digital that, "In August, Russia began striking Ukraine’s border infrastructure along the Moldovan frontier. With Ukrainian grain exports through the Black Sea ports under sustained attack, Moldova has become a transit route for that grain towards Romania’s ports — and the Moldovan government cut rail transit tariffs by half to keep it moving." US WARNS RUSSIAN-LINKED ACTORS SEEKING TO 'FOMENT MANUFACTURED INSURRECTION' IN EUROPEAN COUNTRY These routes, Secrieru said, are a lifeline for Ukraine’s exports and for its economy. "Russia’s strikes are meant to sever them. Russia has also stepped-up violations of Moldova’s airspace in August, to intimidate us into withdrawing our support. Moldova stays the course. We will continue to provide civilian support to Ukraine and to keep the corridors that sustain its economy open," Secrieru told Fox News Digital. President Sandu reported five Russian drones violated its airspace just hours before the country celebrated its independence, in what the president called an attempt at "intimidation." "We have repeatedly warned about the unacceptable risks posed by Russia’s war against Ukraine. Yet another Russian attack on Ukraine has once again resulted in violations of Moldova’s airspace," the foreign ministry posted on X. Secrieru told Fox News Digital that Russia violated Moldovan airspace on 17 occasions in August, the highest number of violations in a month since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy recently visited his Moldovan counterpart in Chișinău, taking part in Independence Day celebrations and emphasizing the shared struggle of Ukrainians and Moldovans in the face of the threat posed by neighboring Russia. "Russia is doing a lot to ruin our lives in Ukraine, to ruin your lives in Moldova, and to make it as difficult as possible for Romania. This is the ‘Russian world.’ It spoils. It destroys. But we will win. I am sure," Zelenskyy told a large Independence Day gathering. ZELENSKYY PRESSURES US AND EUROPE FOR MORE 'AIR DEFENSE' ASSISTANCE AMID ONGOING WAR WITH RUSSIA RUSSIA USES AMMO DEPOT IN TRANSNISTRIA TO SMUGGLE WEAPONS ACROSS UKRAINIAN BORDERS Both Moldova and Ukraine applied for EU membership on the same day, shortly after Russia’s invasion in 2022. Russia’s invasion and its destabilization efforts in Moldova complicate both countries' path forward to EU membership, a central goal of Putin’s Russia as Moscow has tried to stymie the countries of the former Soviet republic from moving closer to the West and EU institutions. Russia’s new threats against its neighbors come on the heels of CIA Director John Ratcliffe’s surprise visit to Moscow, fueling speculation Russia intends to escalate conflict with NATO members, particularly the Baltic nations of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. Along with its kinetic actions in Ukraine and incursions into Moldova’s airspace, Moscow uses influence operations in the former Soviet space to aid pro-Russian actors and push pro-Russian points of view. "Russia has been interfering in Moldova for years, and these latest reports fit the broader pattern of Moscow using hybrid warfare to test how far it can push Europe without triggering a serious response," Ivana Stradner, research fellow with the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital. Moldova remains a prime target for Russian influence operations over 30 years after declaring independence from the Soviet Union. Russia maintains around 1,500 troops in the breakaway territory of Transnistria, which split away from Moldova after the declaration of independence from the Soviet Union in 1991. Stradner, who focuses on Russian disinformation campaigns, said Putin is counting on Western risk aversion and betting that if a country isn’t under the NATO umbrella, the West will decide it’s safer to look away. "That’s exactly why Moldova matters. This could be a rehearsal for how Moscow tests the Baltics," Stradner warned. The Baltic countries are taking notice of what’s happening in Moldova and there are growing fears that Russia may escalate the conflict beyond Ukraine. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna stated on X that while Estonia’s threat assessment has not changed, "Russia’s threat and possible provocations against NATO must be taken seriously." Other Baltic leaders including Latvia’s Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs reiterated that the threat of a Russian invasion remains low but warned of an increased risk of Russian actions. Since independence, Moldova has set its sights on moving closer to the West, with recent elections and a referendum on becoming a member of the European Union gaining significant support.

articles.title: Chicken Shop Date to end as host says 'time to move on'
articles.summary: Amelia Dimoldenberg announces she will end her popular YouTube series after more than a decade.
articles.body:
Amelia Dimoldenberg has announced she will end Chicken Shop Date after more than a decade.

The presenter, known for her off-the-wall questions and deadpan silences, revealed the news in an Instagram post.

She has become one of the UK's best-known content creators through the web series, which features interviews with rappers, actors and celebrities framed as a "date" with the host.

While "all good dates must come to an end", Dimoldenberg told fans to expect "a few final dates" before the show officially ends.

"To me the show is my very own rom-com and I have loved creating so many stories for you to watch," she wrote.

"I am so grateful to everyone who has followed me on this journey and found some joy in these episodes.

"I never thought I'd stop Chicken Shop Date, I thought maybe it would be a part of me forever, and in some way it always will, but I feel like it's now time to move on from this adventure and on to a new one."

Dimoldenberg insisted just months ago she had no plans to end Chicken Shop Date, and said she planned to carry on until she met her "one true love".

Her most recent interviewees have included music heavyweight Paul McCartney, Swedish pop star Zara Larsson and US television host Conan O'Brien.

The presenter has long said her dream guest would be Drake and fans will be speculating if she's managed to bag the Canadian rapper for one of her final episodes.

And thousands of supportive comments have been left under the announcement post.

Radio 1 presenter and podcaster Jamie Laing wrote: "The G.O.A.T."

Author and broadcaster Elizabeth Day wrote: "Knowing when to stop - and leaving on such a high, after shaping the culture - is the quintessential power move."

Rapper Tinie Tempah commented: "Smashed it!"

Dimoldenberg previously told the BBC how Chicken Shop Date had grown out of a series of interviews with grime artists she conducted as a teenager for culture magazine The Cut.

"I started Chicken Shop Date as part of a youth club, and we made a magazine, and everything I learned there, the connections I made, the mentoring I got, set me up for the career that I have today," she said.

The presenter has also been a vocal supporter of training programmes and apprenticeships to help young people into employment.

Yet success hasn't come overnight, as she told BBC Newsbeat last year.

"Some people think it's been, like, two years," she said.

"I spent so much time trying to persuade publicists, managers and talent to come on the show."

The creator said that in 2014, social media wasn't seen as the best place to promote a celebrity's latest album, film or product.

Chicken Shop Date has since gone on to rank alongside platforms like Graham Norton's chatshow or BBC Radio 1 for celebrities seeking media cut-through, she told The Guardian last month.

articles.title: Indonesia fires: Toxic haze spreads across South East Asia amid 'super' El Niño
articles.summary: Millions of people have been exposed to the smog, with more than 12,000 children suffering respiratory issues.
articles.body:
A blanket of toxic haze is enveloping parts of Indonesia and spreading into Malaysia, Singapore and the Philippines, as weeks-long wildfires continue to burn.

Millions of people across large swathes of South East Asia have been exposed to the smog, which in some areas has fuelled "acutely unhealthy" pollution more than 15 times the World Health Organization's recommended level.

Many of the ongoing fires have been burning across Sumatra and Indonesian Borneo since mid-July – underpinned by a so-called Super El Niño that is exacerbating drought conditions.

Between July and August, Indonesia's Health Ministry recorded over 50,000 cases of respiratory infections linked to land and forest fires.

More than 12,000 of those cases are of children under the age of five.

Rizma Nur Fatimah, a 19-year-old teaching assistant at a school in Banjarbaru, South Kalimantan, told the BBC that the smog in her classroom had become so thick "you couldn't even see your own feet".

"Even inside the house, with everything closed, the haze still got in," she said. "We've been living with this since I was born. It's the same every year, so we've almost become resigned to it. But this year is worse."

Misbah, a 23-year-old mother from nearby Pengayuan village, said her three-year-old daughter had developed "a cough, a sore throat and a runny nose" during the haze.

Some 1,300 kilometres away, in the Philippine island province of Palawan, residents reported similar symptoms, including itchy eyes, nose and throat.

"We are now experiencing mild headaches," said Dr Precious Bañas-Melad. "My cousin who isn't allergic to anything started developing allergies. My husband is the first one who had itchy eyes and throat."

Malaysia, meanwhile, has reported rising cases of asthma and conjunctivitis amid worsening air quality nationwide as smoke continues to drift across the border.

Indonesia's forest and peatland fires are not a new phenomenon. Experts say the crisis is rooted in decades of land-use change, dating back to the Suharto era, when vast areas of rainforest and peatland in Kalimantan were opened for logging, plantations and large-scale development projects.

Today, large-scale fires are often associated with the expansion of industrial plantations and other commercial land use. Environmental groups, researchers, and government investigations have repeatedly alleged that some companies use fire as a cheap and effective way to clear vast areas of land.

Some point out that while drought and El Niño conditions help fires spread, the severity of the haze is also linked to human activity. Drained peatlands, industrial timber estates and oil palm plantations can leave landscapes more vulnerable to burning, with fires often recurring in the same areas.

Unlike traditional practices, which are small-scale, community-managed, and closely monitored, fires linked to large-scale land development can be far more difficult to control and can cause environmental and public health impacts on a much larger scale.

What makes Indonesian Borneo's wildfires particularly worrying is that they are burning through one of the world's largest tropical peatland ecosystems.

Under normal conditions, these peatlands serve as gigantic carbon reservoirs. But under abnormal conditions, such as those currently hitting the region, they can become carbon "bombs".

UN warns of 'supersized' El Niño as countries prepare for impact

Orangutans in danger as wildfires blaze through Indonesia

"Peatlands are incredibly effective carbon stores because their waterlogged conditions slow decomposition, allowing carbon to accumulate underground for thousands of years," explains Dr Nisa Novita, a peatland researcher at Indonesian conservation NGO Yayasan Konservasi Alam Nusantara.

"But this also means they can become a 'carbon bomb' when they are drained or burned, because that carbon can be rapidly released into the atmosphere."

Others have warned that as the current Super El Niño continues to escalate over the coming months, the fires could significantly worsen.

Last year, without El Niño, forest fires in Indonesia torched a 359,000-hectare area, says Professor Bambang Hero Saharjo, a forest fire forensics expert from Institut Pertanian Bogor University.

Citing research reports, Prof Bambang told the BBC that this year's El Niño could burn an area as large as 11 million hectares – putting it on par with one of Indonesia's worst wildfire seasons, which happened from 1997 to 1998.

Earlier this week, Indonesia's forestry minister Raja Juli Antoni told reporters that the battle to extinguish the current wildfires was entering a critical phase.

"Our problems are not over. September is the peak of El Niño," he said earlier this week. "September is the main fight for us."
authors: BBC Indonesian, Gavin Butler and Virma Simonette

articles.title: Vietnam court sentences 11 to death in drug trafficking case
articles.summary: More than 200 people are convicted over a network smuggling drugs into Vietnam in toothpaste tubes and other consumer items.
articles.body:
Eleven people have been sentenced to death by a court in Vietnam in one of the country's largest drug trafficking cases, state media report.

They are among 227 people accused in total, with prison sentences ranging from 18 months to life behind bars.

Among those sentenced to death was the person purported to be the mastermind behind the drug trafficking network, Ha Danh Nam, who investigators said arranged for the drugs to be brought from France to Vietnam.

The case began in March 2023 when four Vietnam Airlines flight attendants - arriving in Ho Chi Minh City from Paris - were caught carrying more than 10kg of drugs in 157 toothpaste tubes.

Legal affairs newspaper Bao Cong Ly reported that authorities found the flight attendants - who were not prosecuted - had unknowingly transported the drugs, which included MDMA and ketamine.

Nam was found to have hidden the drugs inside consumer goods - including dietary supplements, laundry detergent, mouthwash and coffee - and then arranged for people in France to carry them in their luggage or transported via delivery service to Vietnam.

Nam targeted Vietnamese nationals living or studying in France to act as drug mules, local media report.

Prosecutors said those involved in this transnational drug trafficking network used encrypted messaging platforms and bank accounts registered under other people's names to facilitate their smuggling efforts.

Transactions linked to the network were worth nearly 29 trillion Vietnamese dong ($1.1bn; £815m), they said.

The court found the defendants played varying roles in the network - from leaders to accomplices - and penalties were imposed according to the seriousness of their involvement.

Around 20 others on trial were sentenced to life imprisonment for the illegal buying, selling, transporting and organising of drugs.

Vietnam is one of 54 countries that still have the death penalty, rights groups say.

The government does not publish how many people are on death row as that is considered a state secret, though human rights groups say there are more than 1,000 awaiting execution.

Last month, the Vietnamese government proposed abolishing the death penalty for six offences including drug trafficking. These proposed changes are yet to take effect.

The proposal follows changes to the criminal code in 2025 that removed the death penalty for eight offences - including embezzlement, espionage and overthrowing the government.

One of the most high-profile figures to be handed the death penalty was tycoon Truong My Lan, who was found guilty of embezzlement and sentenced to death in 2024.

The 2025 change in the law led to her death penalty being commuted to life imprisonment .

articles.title: Feminist icon Gloria Steinem dies aged 92
articles.summary: Cofounder of Ms Magazine was a strong advocate for women’s rights throughout her life.
articles.body:
Gloria Steinem, the author and activist who became one of the most visible symbols and potent voices of the women’s movement in the United States and a fierce advocate for feminist causes throughout her life, has died at the age of 92.

With her trademark streaked hair parted down the middle and large aviator glasses, Steinem, a cofounder of Ms Magazine, was a hugely recognisable presence wherever she went.

And she went everywhere: much of her life as an advocate was spent on the road, speaking at college campuses and community centres, at rallies and marches.

She died on Wednesday at her home in New York City, according to her foundation’s social media pages.

“Gloria’s greatest gift was her ability to listen to others, to make others feel seen and heard,” the posts said. “Her words, actions, and example gave people permission to be their truest selves. Gloria lived true to her independent spirit, always with curiosity and a great sense of humour.”

Steinem enjoyed writing and spending time in the community in recent years, the posts said. She also hosted talking circles for hundreds of people in her home.

“You can’t do it on the phone or on the web,” she told The Associated Press news agency in a 2015 interview.

“You have to be there with all five senses. It should be obvious that people can’t empathise with each other unless we’re in the same room.”

Steinem began her career as a journalist, notably one who reported, in 1963, on degrading conditions in Hugh Hefner’s Playboy empire, an undercover assignment she later came to regret.

She credits a meeting six years later, where women spoke out boldly in favour of abortion rights, with changing her career path.

“That speak-out was the beginning of activism for me,” Steinem, who had undergone a secret illegal abortion herself at age 22, told the AP in an email in 2022, reflecting on the reversal of Roe v Wade.

“Either our control over our own bodies is equal, regardless of sex or race, or we’re not living in a democracy.”

Though she soon became a known activist, those who watched Steinem denounce discrimination for so many years likely never suspected that she’d had to overcome a deep fear of public speaking. She would have simply stuck to writing, she said, if only editors at the time had been willing to let her write about the women’s movement.

Time hardly slowed Steinem down; well into her 80s she was travelling the globe and speaking out on issues of importance to her. These included everything from genital mutilation to Korean reconciliation, but it was equality for women that took precedence.

articles.title: Nvidia to buy Hugging Face for nearly $13 billion in big bet on open AI models
articles.summary: Nvidia will buy popular developer platform Hugging Face for $12.93 billion, betting that support for open AI models will drive future demand even as its biggest customers develop their own chips to reduce reliance on the semiconductor giant.
articles.body: Nvidia will buy popular developer platform Hugging Face for $12.93 billion, betting that support for open AI models will drive future demand even as its biggest customers develop their own chips to reduce reliance on the semiconductor giant. Shares of the company were slightly lower after the deal on Thursday, which ranks among its biggest ever. The chipmaker is already a major open AI player in the U.S. with its widely used Nemotron model and vocal support for the technology. Acquiring Hugging Face will give it direct access to a platform developers use to collaborate, test and share tools, potentially providing valuable insight and data that could help it narrow the technology gap with top American and Chinese labs. Demand for open-weight models has surged from businesses balking at the steep bill of deploying the technology, with Chinese companies such as DeepSeek and Z.ai emerging as crucial players with models that can match the best from the United States in tasks including generating computer code at a lower cost. That surge has fueled fears that some American firms could become reliant on Beijing’s models even as both countries race to dominate a technology they see as crucial to their future. “Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem,” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said, adding that his company’s chips will not be required to build on or deploy through Hugging Face. Under the deal, Nvidia will pay about $11.9 billion to Hugging Face investors, while offering an equity-based retention program of up to $1 billion for employees who join Nvidia. For Nvidia, building up open source may help it cushion a demand slowdown from customers such as Meta, OpenAI and Microsoft, which are developing their own AI chips to cut reliance on its costly and supply-constrained processors. Hugging Face has also been in the news recently after a hack by rogue AI agents that escaped OpenAI’s testing environment. Beyond hosting AI models, it offers datasets, software libraries and cloud services used to build and deploy AI applications. The New York-based startup, which is backed by Intel, Advanced Micro Devices and Amazon, was founded in 2016 by French entrepreneurs Clément Delangue, Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf.

articles.title: Tens of thousands flood streets to protest Spain border crisis
articles.summary: Tens of thousands protested Pedro Sanchez across Spain as 50,000 marched in Madrid over the migrant crisis in Ceuta following July's border surge.
articles.body: Tens of thousands of people took to the streets across Spain to protest the government's handling of a mass crossing of migrants into Spain in July. Authorities say 50,000 protesters were on the streets in Madrid alone, furious at Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez as the migrant crisis in Spain's north African city of Ceuta continues. Violence continued for hours after the major protests ended, with gunshots and explosions audible throughout the night on Wednesday. SPAIN STOCKS AFRICAN ENCLAVE CEUTA WITH BOOSTED SECURITY AS MOROCCO MONITORS CALLS FOR SECOND BORDER RUSH The protesters bore signs reading, "A united Ceuta will never be defeated," "Sánchez to prison," and "Invaders — go home!" Spain is still dealing with the fallout after over 70,000 foreign migrants surged across its border from neighboring Morocco in late July. AT LEAST 72 DEAD AMID MASS MIGRANT RUSH TO STORM SPANISH ENCLAVE OF CEUTA SPARKING BORDER CRISIS Thousands of those migrants remain in Spanish territory even now. "What happened to us was not a migratory crisis," Ceuta's regional leader, Juan Jesús Vivas, said Wednesday. "What happened was the violation of Spain's territorial integrity." SOCIALIST SPANISH PM BLASTS MELONI OVER RESTORED BORDER CONTROLS AFTER CEUTA SURGE, DEMANDS EMERGENCY MEETING The protests came days after Ceuta residents tore down and burned makeshift migrant shelters found in their city. Demonstrators carrying Spanish flags moved toward beachside migrant camps last week, destroying shelters and setting fires as police attempted to keep protesters and migrants apart, according to Spain’s public broadcaster RTVE and news agency EFE. SPAIN DEPLOYS MILITARY AFTER THOUSANDS OF MIGRANTS OVERWHELM BORDER ENCLAVE, AT LEAST 18 DEAD Meanwhile, Sanchez has blamed Russia and Israel for amplifying the migrant crisis via social media, saying the July surge across the border was due to a misinterpretation of a Spanish Supreme Court ruling. Sánchez told radio station SER that research by the European Union’s diplomatic service, the European External Action Service, indicated Russian and Israeli networks had participated in spreading disinformation alongside far-right networks, Reuters reported Aug. 31. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar accused Sánchez of "lying shamelessly," and said in a post on X that the Spanish leader was attempting to divert attention from domestic policy failures.
